# Settings reference

<!-- GENERATED by scripts/gen_settings_reference.py from the help texts in
     crates/reco-gui/ui/main.slint. Do not edit by hand: change the tip in the
     Slint file and re-run the script. -->

Every setting below is shown in the app with a **?** badge that displays the
same text. Defaults are the values the app starts with before any saved
setup or preference overrides them. A blank default means the value is
filled in by the app (for example from the loaded setup). Picking a
**Style preset** in the AI Tracking section overwrites the framing sliders,
so their defaults only apply until you pick one.

## Seam

| Setting | Range | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| Seam blend | 0 to 0.3 | 0.05 | Width of the feathered blend at the seam between the two cameras. |
| Flip blend direction (left over right) |  | off | Which camera fades in over the other at the seam. Off (default): right fades over a fixed left. On: left fades over a fixed right. Doesn't move the seam itself. |
| Multi-band blend |  | on (new setups) | Spatial (multi-band) blend: blurs low frequencies over a wide band and keeps high frequencies over a narrow band, instead of a single crossfade. Lets the seam blend read as wider without doubling fine detail (ball, player edges, field lines) - but costs 10 render passes instead of 1. |
| Show seam line |  | off | Draws a thin red line at the exact geometric seam position, independent of how wide the seam blend is. Purely a visual aid for tuning Seam position and Flip blend direction - doesn't affect the render otherwise. |
| Overlap view |  |  | Calibration aid, preview only (never in an export). Right over left / Left over right: shows that camera semi-transparently on the other camera's side of the seam - where the calibration is right, lines and goals line up; where it's off, you see them doubled. Difference: shows how much the two cameras differ wherever both see the same spot - near black = aligned, bright edges = misaligned. Both: both ghosts at once across the whole overlap - lines that cross the seam at an angle point to a roll error. Judge on far-away things (far touchline, goals); close to the cameras some doubling is normal (parallax). |
| Overlap opacity | 0.0 to 1.0 | 0.5 | Ghost: how strongly the other camera shows through. Difference: how much of the difference image replaces the normal picture. |
| Seam position | -0.3 to 0.3 | 0.0 | Moves the seam left/right by hand, independent of calibration - safe to drag freely, unlike Intersect (which can open a black gap if pushed too far). Or drag directly on the preview while Show seam line is on. |

## Rig Alignment

| Setting | Range | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| Rig tilt | -30 to 30 | 0.0 | Forward/backward lean of the camera rig; straightens vertical lines at the panorama edges. |
| Rig roll | -15 to 15 | 0.0 | Side-to-side tilt of the camera rig. |

### Detection Zones

| Setting | Range | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| Show AI pitch limits |  | off | Draws two draggable lines on the stitched preview marking how far up/down the AI camera may aim - a manual safety margin to keep it away from the black-wedge seam area. Doesn't affect manual panning, only AI tracking. |

### Scoreboard

| Setting | Range | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| Auto-cut lead-in + pauses |  | off | Adds cut ranges for the dead time before kickoff and any logged pause, keeping the seconds of context set below at each boundary. Only from period_start(1)/pause_start/pause_end events actually in the log - won't guess at a break you forgot to mark with Pause. Doesn't touch cut ranges you added or edited by hand. |
| Pause cut |  |  | Seconds of play kept around every cut-out pause: before it, so the incident that stopped play is still in the export, and after it, so the restart is not cut into. |
| Match trim |  |  | Seconds kept outside the match itself: lead-in before kickoff, and how long the export keeps running past the final whistle. These two move the export start/end time, not a cut range. |
| Highlights only (goals) |  | off | Export only the goals: one clip per logged goal, spliced together. Sets the export start, end and cut ranges for you, and renames the output so it cannot overwrite the full match. Turning this on turns auto-cut off - it already excludes everything that is not a goal. |
| Goal clip |  |  | How much of each goal to keep. The lead reaches back further than the trail on purpose: the goal is logged after the ball is in, so the build-up sits before the logged moment while only the celebration follows it. |

## Calibration

### Global Parameters

| Setting | Range | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| Intersect | -1.0 to 1.0 | 0.0 | Overlap between the two camera planes; controls how much of each image is used. |
| Camera axis offset | -0.6 to 0.6 | 0.0 | Distance of the virtual camera from the stitch origin; affects parallax at the seam. |

### Left Camera

| Setting | Range | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| Roll | -0.3 to 0.3 | 0.0 | In-plane roll of the left camera's content (z_rx): the image turns around its own viewing axis, like rotating a picture frame, without skewing. This is the roll auto-calibrate solves by default - use this to fine-tune by hand instead of (or after) re-running auto-calibrate. |
| Skew | -0.3 to 0.3 | 0.0 | Tips the left camera's plane forward/backward around its own horizontal axis (z_rz). Because you view that plane at an angle, this reads on screen as a skew/keystone, not as a turn. Manual control for the same angle the "Force extra skew fit (z_rz)" checkbox below lets auto-calibrate solve for. |
| Near-field Tilt | -0.3 to 0.3 | 0.0 | Same as ground_tilt_x, for the left camera's content (z-plane). |
| Far-field Tilt | -0.3 to 0.3 | 0.0 | Same as top_tilt_x, for the left camera's content (z-plane). |

### Right Camera

| Setting | Range | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| Vertical Shift | -0.1 to 0.1 | 0.0 | Vertical alignment correction between the two camera planes. |
| Roll | -0.3 to 0.3 | 0.0 | In-plane roll of the right camera's content (x_rz): the image turns around its own viewing axis, like rotating a picture frame, without skewing. It pivots on the seam edge, so the seam stays put. This is the roll auto-calibrate solves by default - use this to fine-tune by hand instead of (or after) re-running auto-calibrate. |
| Skew | -0.3 to 0.3 | 0.0 | Tips the right camera's plane forward/backward around its own horizontal axis (x_rx). Because you view that plane at an angle, this reads on screen as a skew/keystone, not as a turn. Manual control for the same angle the "Force extra skew fit (x_rx)" checkbox below lets auto-calibrate solve for. |
| Near-field Tilt | -0.3 to 0.3 | 0.0 | Near-field ground-plane tilt correction for the right camera's content (x-plane). Fixes a seam step in ground lines close to the camera that the flat two-plane model can't otherwise correct - only affects the bottom of frame, close to the camera; leaves everything else untouched. |
| Far-field Tilt | -0.3 to 0.3 | 0.0 | Top-of-frame tilt correction for the right camera's content (x-plane). Mirror of ground_tilt_x, for far background content (distant structures, goal frames, skyline) instead of the near field - only affects the top of frame; leaves the ground band untouched. Manual only - no auto-fit yet. |

### Band Width

| Setting | Range | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| Near-tilt | 0.09 to 0.4 | 0.16 | How far into the frame ground_tilt_x/z's correction extends before reaching full strength (the ramp always starts at the same fixed point close to the seam). Wider spreads the correction more gradually; narrower concentrates it closer to the very bottom edge. Shared by both ground_tilt_x and ground_tilt_z. |
| Far-tilt | 0.09 to 0.4 | 0.16 | Same as ground_tilt_band_width, for top_tilt_x/z's band (top of frame instead of the bottom). |

## Color Mapping

| Setting | Range | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| Overlap fit (sky + grass) |  | on (new setups) | Measures both cameras at exactly the same spots next to the seam - from the sky down to the near touchline - and fits a brightness + contrast correction per color channel, so sky and grass can both match (the classic auto match compares a different piece of the field per camera and can only shift the average). When on, the band width / grid / max offset settings and Auto gamma below are not used. |

### Manual Gamma (Before Auto Match)

| Setting | Range | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| Auto gamma (dynamic) |  | off | Continuously re-fits the two gamma values below from the same seam-band measurement the automatic match already uses, on the same interval, instead of holding them at a fixed manual value. A flat additive correction alone can't fix a real sensor-gain (ISO) mismatch between the cameras - that's what manual gamma is for - but a value tuned to fix a large mismatch at one moment can overshoot (visibly reverse the mismatch) once lighting changes later in the same match. This tracks it automatically instead. The sliders below still work while this is on, but any value you set gets overwritten at the next remeasure - turn this off first to set a fixed value that sticks. |
| Gamma left | 0.5 to 2.0 | 1.0 | Left camera's gamma, applied before the automatic match measures anything. Above 1.0 lifts the mid-tones, below 1.0 lowers them. Use this when the two cameras differ in contrast rather than in overall brightness - the automatic match can only shift the average, not reshape the curve. Applies in the preview and in every export, whichever decode path is used. Updates live. |
| Gamma right | 0.5 to 2.0 | 1.0 | Right camera's gamma. See "Gamma left" - set the two against each other until the two halves match in the mid-tones, then let the automatic match take care of what is left. |
| Auto color match |  | on | Periodically measures each camera's color in the seam-adjacent band of its raw frame and nudges both toward their shared average, so an exposure/white-balance mismatch between the two cameras doesn't show up as a color step at the seam. Independent of geometric alignment. Works in the preview and in hardware-decode (zero-copy) exports alike. |

### Measurement

| Setting | Range | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| MEAS Band Width | 0.02 to 1.0 | 0.15 | Width of the seam-adjacent band sampled for the measurement, independent of the seam blend width. Updates live. |
| Measure interval | 1 to 120 | 15 | Re-measure color every N rendered frames. Updates live. |
| Grid columns | 2 to 32 | 8 | Sample grid columns per camera. More = a more stable measurement, at a small extra cost. Updates live. |
| Grid rows | 2 to 64 | 16 | Sample grid rows per camera. Updates live. |

### Correction Limits

| Setting | Range | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| Max Y offset | 0 to 0.2 | 0.06 | Max luma (brightness) correction either camera can receive. Updates live. |
| Max chroma offset | 0 to 0.15 | 0.04 | Max color (chroma) correction either camera can receive. Updates live. |
| Smoothing (EMA alpha) | 0.01 to 1.0 | 0.15 | How fast the correction reacts to a new measurement (higher = faster, noisier). Updates live. |
| Remeasure now |  |  | Force a fresh color-match measurement against the current frame right now, instead of waiting for the next periodic remeasure - useful while paused, or right after seeking to a frame with different lighting. |

### Vivid Color Grade

| Setting | Range | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| Vivid |  | off | Universal color grade applied to the whole composited output - perks up grey/dull footage. Sets brightness/saturation/gamma to a tuned preset; use the sliders below to fine-tune further, or leave this off and drive the sliders directly. 1.0/1.0/1.0 is identity - off by default, no GPU cost. Updates live and is saved in the setup. |
| Brightness | 0.5 to 1.5 | 1.0 | Color grade brightness multiplier. 1.0 is identity - above brightens, below darkens. Updates live. |
| Saturation | 0.5 to 1.5 | 1.0 | Color grade saturation multiplier. 1.0 is identity - above makes colors more vivid, below desaturates toward greyscale. Updates live. |
| Gamma | 0.5 to 1.5 | 1.0 | Color grade gamma. 1.0 is identity - above lifts mid-tones, below lowers them. Updates live. |

### Dehaze

| Setting | Range | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| Dehaze | 0.0 to 0.8 | 0.0 | Removes the grey veil of fog or haze from the far side of the pitch, the stand and the background, bringing back their colour and contrast. The near field is left as it is: the effect grows with distance from the camera. The fog colour is measured from the sky, so it needs some sky in view to start. 0.35-0.5 suits a misty day; higher brings up compression noise in the distance. 0.0 (default) disables it - no GPU cost. GPU-only. Updates live and is saved in the setup. |
| Keep brightness | 0.0 to 1.0 | 0.5 | Shown when Dehaze is above 0. How much of the brightness the fog removal takes away is given back. Thick fog: set it high (around 1.0), otherwise the picture gets too dark. Thin fog: set it low (around 0.0), because giving brightness back there makes the picture look milky. 0.5 (default) is in between. Updates live and is saved in the setup. |

### Sharpening

| Setting | Range | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| Sharpening | 0.0 to 2.0 | 0.0 | Unsharp-mask sharpening applied to the final output, compensating for detail loss when the AI panner zooms into a crop of the panorama. 0.0 (default) disables it - no GPU cost. Above ~1.5 starts showing visible haloing around high-contrast edges. GPU-only. Updates live and is saved in the setup. |
| Radius |  |  | Blur sample radius in pixels. Larger sharpens coarser detail (useful when heavily zoomed in); smaller targets fine detail. |

## Advanced

### Sampling

| Setting | Range | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| Anchor frame: |  |  | Frame number to center calibration sampling on. Leave empty to use the current playback position instead. |
| Sample window | 0 to 120 | 0.0 | Keep all calibration sample frames within this many seconds of the anchor frame above (or the current playback position, if it's empty), instead of spreading them across the rest of the clip. Use it to point Re-calibrate at a moment with lots of texture on the field (people, cones, ...). 0 = off. |

### Feature Detection

| Setting | Range | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| AKAZE threshold | 0.00005 to 0.005 | 0.0001 | Feature detector sensitivity. Lower = more (weaker) features detected. Updates the preview live. |
| Detect Y min | 0 to 0.5 | 0.05 | Top edge of the vertical region used for feature detection (fraction of frame height). Updates the preview live. |
| Detect Y max | 0.5 to 1.0 | 0.95 | Bottom edge of the vertical region used for feature detection (fraction of frame height). Updates the preview live. |
| Full-resolution features (slower) |  | off | Detect features at full video resolution instead of downscaling to 1920px wide. More precise on 4K+ footage, but slower. |

### Pixel Refine

| Setting | Range | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| Refine alignment on pixels |  | on | After the feature-point fit, fine-tune the alignment by comparing what both cameras actually show along the seam (lines, fences, boards, players). Fixes steps in lines and doubled players near the camera. Adds about two minutes. |

### Rig Level

| Setting | Range | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| Level the rig from vertical structures |  | on | Set Rig tilt and Rig roll from vertical structures in the footage (light masts, goal posts, fence posts, buildings, standing players) instead of the cameras' motion sensors. Needs some vertical structures in view; if there are too few, tilt and roll stay as they were. |

### Skew Fit

| Setting | Range | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| Force extra skew fit (x_rx) |  | off | Solve the right camera's independent skew (x_rx, the "Skew" slider above), even without IMU data. Normally only auto-enabled when the IMU detects >2 deg differential pitch - cameras without a native gyro never get that seed. Try this if the two images still look rotated relative to each other after calibrating. |
| Force extra skew fit (z_rz) |  | off | Solve the left camera's independent skew (z_rz, the "Skew" slider above). There's no IMU signal for this angle, so it's always off unless checked here. Try this if the stitch still looks skewed after enabling Force extra skew fit (x_rx). |

## Export dialog

### Export tab

| Setting | Range | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| Output file |  |  | Destination for the stitched export. Type a path directly or browse - whatever's here when you click Start Export is used verbatim. |
| Resolution |  |  | Output resolution for the stitched video. Independent of the source cameras' resolution. |
| Codec |  |  | Video codec for the export. Falls back automatically (hardware -> software) if a specific encoder can't be opened on this machine - check the Debug log for which one was actually used. |
| Quality |  |  | Encoder quality preset - trades encode speed and file size for visual quality. The numbers are the target and peak bitrate the hardware (NVENC) encoder uses for the chosen codec and resolution; the software fallback encoders are quality-based (CRF) and have no fixed bitrate. |
| Processing range |  |  | Trims the export to a start/end time window within the loaded clip. Defaults to the full clip. |
| Start (s) |  |  | Export start time, in seconds from the beginning of the clip. |
| End (s) |  |  | Export end time, in seconds from the beginning of the clip. |
| Cut ranges |  |  | Excludes a time range from the export, splicing what remains back together with no gap. Drag the reddish band on the scrubber above, or use "+ Add cut" and edit the numbers here. |
| PAUZE overlay on cuts |  | off | Shows a "PAUZE" dip-to-black transition at every cut range above, instead of an instant content jump. No effect with no cut ranges. |
| Fade |  |  | Fade: how long the dip to black and back takes. It is drawn over footage that was going to be encoded anyway, so it adds no length to the export. Black: how long the picture stays fully black on "PAUZE" - the only part that lengthens the export, and the number to raise if a pause should read as a real break. |
| Record replay (stacked raw input for re-stitching) |  | off | Also saves the raw pre-stitch source frames (stacked side-by-side) to a separate file alongside the export, for later re-stitching without re-decoding the originals. |
| Save AI debug events (.jsonl for visualize_detections.py) |  | off | Writes every detection, filter decision, and pan decision to a .jsonl file next to the export, for offline analysis with visualize_detections.py. |

### AI tracking

| Setting | Range | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| Enable |  | off | Turns on AI camera tracking (ball/player detection) for this export. Needs a YOLO ONNX model below. |
| Tracking mode |  |  | Field: follows the player cluster + ball together (falls back to ball-only if the model has no player class). Ball: follows only the ball. Sweep: a fixed left-right pan with no AI at all - a baseline/debug mode. |
| Detect every N frames |  |  | Runs AI detection every Nth frame; frames in between reuse the last detection. Higher = cheaper but staler positions during fast action. |
| Ball anchor range | 0.1 to 0.8 | 0.20 | Before the panner ever sees a ball position, the ball tracker itself requires a raw detection to be within this distance of at least one tracked player - farther detections are dropped as likely false positives (crowd, background). This runs ahead of Ball reach below, so a genuine isolated ball (e.g. a breakaway) can be silently discarded here even with Ball reach raised. Widen it if the panner never even coasts onto a real, far-from-the-pack ball. |
| Ball coast time | 0.2 to 15.0 | 0.67 | A ball leaving the field ROI looks identical to the tracker as "no detection this frame" - the ROI filter drops it before the tracker ever sees it. A ball already being tracked keeps holding its last known position for up to this long before the track is declared lost, same as any other brief detection gap - long enough to bridge a throw-in or a ball briefly rolling out of bounds and being brought back. A ball never tracked in the first place (e.g. a kid's ball just outside the pitch) never starts this countdown, so raising it doesn't make the panner more likely to trigger on that. |
| Ball hold time | 0.0 to 15.0 | 0.0 | After the tracker gives up on the ball, keep the camera pointed at its last known position for this long instead of swinging back to the players. A ball that disappears is usually just briefly undetected and comes back close to where it vanished - measured on real footage within half a frame width in 65-91% of cases - so swinging away only to return reads as the camera drifting off and coming back. Holding keeps the shot still and the camera is already in the right place when the ball returns. Works on top of "Ball coast time": that one decides how long the tracker keeps reporting a position, this one how long the camera keeps using the last one afterwards. Set to 0 for the old behaviour. |
| Ball max speed | 0.0 to 0.5 | 0.13 | Stops the camera jumping to a different ball - a warm-up or neighbouring-pitch ball that is detected just as confidently as your own. A real ball cannot cross the pitch between two frames, so any "move" faster than this is treated as a different ball and ignored. Measured on real footage this removed every rapid back-and-forth flip between two balls. The allowance grows while the ball is missing, so a ball that was genuinely lost for a moment can still be picked up again anywhere. Lower = stricter. Set to 0 to switch the check off. |
| Player height limit | 0.0 to 0.6 | 0.0 | Ignores people higher up in the picture than your own pitch reaches, when the camera decides where the action is. If a neighbouring field is in view, everyone warming up over there is detected as a player too and can easily outnumber your match - on the test footage 94% of all detected people were on the other field, so the camera followed THAT group and your own ball was only in frame 16% of the time. Cutting them out moved the camera from 47 to 13 degrees off your ball. Set to 0 to count everyone. Use an AI Debug export to see where your own far touchline sits. |
| Ball height limit | 0.0 to 0.6 | 0.0 | Ignores balls that sit higher up in the picture than your own pitch reaches - typically a ball being played on a neighbouring field behind yours, which is further away and so appears higher and smaller. On the test match this removed every jump to the wrong ball. WARNING: raise this carefully. Play on the far side of your OWN pitch also sits high in the picture, so a value that is too low will make the camera ignore real play at the far end. Start at 0 (off), then lower it only as far as needed. Check an AI Debug export to see how high your own far touchline sits. |
| Ball jump confidence | 0.0 to 0.95 | 0.5 | How sure the AI must be about a ball that suddenly appears far from where the ball was, before the tracker will follow it. Weak, flickering detections on the far side of the pitch no longer drag the camera along, while a clear detection still does. Works together with "Ball max speed"; that one is the stronger guard. Set to 0 to switch this check off. |
| Ball acquire range | 0.0 to 3.0 | 0.0 | Guards against locking onto a ball that isn't part of this match - a warm-up or neighbouring-pitch ball that drifts into the field ROI. "Ball anchor range" can't catch that on its own, because the kids playing with that ball are tracked people too, so the ball looks properly anchored. This limits how far from the main group of players a brand-new ball track may START. It never restricts a ball that is already being tracked: a breakaway, a long clearance or a goal kick still gets followed anywhere, and a coasting ball still holds the aim. Set to 0 to switch the whole check off. |
| Ball acquire arm delay | 0 to 300 | 45 | How many tracked frames the ball must be held before "Ball acquire range" starts applying. Until then any acquisition is allowed, so the first ball of the match - a kickoff, always from the centre circle - is never blocked. After the tracker has proven it can hold the real ball this long, a brand-new track appearing far from everyone is far more likely to be somebody else's ball. Only matters when "Ball acquire range" is above 0. |
| Detection confidence | 0.05 to 0.9 | 0.10 | A raw detection - person, ball, or referee - below this score never reaches the tracker at all. Raise it if a weak, noisy detection (e.g. a stray low-confidence "ball" on background clutter) visibly yanks the camera; lower it if the model is missing a real but faint detection. Applies to every class and every tracking mode alike - Ball tracking mode no longer silently uses a higher floor of its own. |
| Style preset |  |  | One-shot preset that overwrites every slider below (framing, cluster mode, lock-pitch, bandwidth, dead-zone, ball weight, FOV) with tuned defaults for that style. You can still tweak any slider afterward. |
| Framing |  |  | Action: aims at the (optionally confidence-weighted) player cluster, with ball pull and dynamic zoom. Frame all: aims at the geometric center of every player, zoomed to fit the whole team. |
| Lock (horizontal-only) |  | off | Holds the camera's tilt fixed and pans left/right only. Off by default - the camera follows the action's vertical position too. |
| Lookahead (smoothness) | 0.0 to 2.5 | 1.5 | Buffers N seconds of future frames so the panner can smooth over past+future and lead the action slightly, instead of reacting frame-by-frame. The dominant lever for smooth AI panning. 0 disables it. |
| Reduce lookahead memory (8-bit) |  | off | Buffers the lookahead at 8-bit instead of the source's native bit depth, roughly halving its VRAM cost on 10-bit footage (e.g. DJI Action 4 HEVC) - lets a longer lookahead fit on lower-VRAM cards. No effect on already-8-bit sources. The same buffered frames feed the final render too, so this trades a little gradient smoothness (sky, grass, floodlit surfaces) for memory. Currently also REQUIRED for 10-bit sources, not just a VRAM fallback - leaving it off crashes with a known wgpu texture-copy bug, fix pending. |
| Async AI detection (faster export) |  | off | Runs AI detection's inference call on a background thread instead of blocking the export loop - AI detection is typically the single biggest export-speed bottleneck. Measured 1.2-1.4x faster export across multiple test runs (no change to detection results, purely a timing change - see docs/async-detect-benchmark-v054.md). Costs a real but modest extra ~400MB VRAM (a second loaded model instance), not a doubling of the whole session. Only affects the buffered/export loop (needs Lookahead > 0). Off by default - turn on if your card has VRAM headroom to spare. |

### Advanced panner

| Setting | Range | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| Cluster mode |  |  | Density (default): follows the tightest knot of players, ignoring stragglers. Trimmed mean: averages all players' positions, trimming outliers - a distant group can still pull the aim before trimming kicks in. |
| Ball weight | 0.0 to 1.0 | 0.20 | How strongly the ball pulls the aim away from the player cluster (Action framing only) - scaled by ball confidence and distance from the cluster. Forced to 1.0 in Ball tracking mode. |
| Cluster bandwidth | 0.1 to 0.6 | 0.30 | Radius used by Density cluster mode to group nearby players. Wider pulls a looser formation into one cluster; narrower isolates a tight core. No effect in Trimmed mean mode. |
| Dead-zone | 0.0 to 0.5 | 0.20 | Camera holds still while the target stays within this radius; larger errors ease in beyond it instead of snapping. Removes micro-wobble on static play - relies on Lookahead to absorb the added latency. |
| Ball reach | 0.0 to 1.5 | 0.5 | How far the ball may stray from the player cluster and still pull the aim (Action framing only). Beyond this the ball is treated as off-the-action - a stray detection or the far goal - and ignored. Raise it if the camera won't follow a real ball that's broken away from the pack, e.g. into a corner. |
| Field of view (degrees) |  |  | Bounds for the panner's continuously-varying zoom, recomputed every frame from cluster spread and framing. Default is just the starting FOV before any players are detected. |
| Ball margin | 0.0 to 15.0 | 3.0 | How much room is kept between the ball and the edge of the frame. The zoom widens until the ball sits at least this far inside the picture, so it is never flush against the border. Larger keeps more air around the ball (the camera zooms out sooner); smaller lets it drift closer to the edge. This only sets a floor on the zoom - it never pans the camera - and Wide above still caps it, so a ball far outside the Wide field of view leaves frame regardless. |
| Zoom range |  |  | The boxes show what the panner frames at its widest and tightest zoom, drawn on the current preview frame. The thin grey box is Default: the shot the camera opens on before it has detected anyone, not a third limit - the zoom leaves it as soon as tracking starts. Sizes are relative to the preview's own field of view, so they move if you zoom the preview itself. The upscale figure under each is how far the render is pushed past what the lens actually resolves: above roughly 1.5x the picture starts to look soft no matter which encoder settings you pick. |
| Smoothing speed |  |  | How fast the panner's smoothed values (not the raw target) catch up each frame - an exponential-moving-average rate, not a delay. Low = calm but laggy; a brief, fast-moving ball can leave frame before the camera/zoom ever catches up, even with Ball reach and FOV Wide raised. High = snappier but can reintroduce the wobble those settings were tuned to avoid - raise gradually. |
| Zoom (FOV) | 0.005 to 0.3 | 0.01 | How fast the dynamic zoom catches up to its computed target FOV. Default 0.01 has a ~3s time constant at 30fps - often too slow to reach a wide enough shot before a brief breakaway is over. |
| Aim (cluster) | 0.005 to 0.3 | 0.012 | How fast the aim point catches up to the player cluster centroid. Default 0.012, same slow-time-constant caveat as Zoom. |

### AI Debug tab

| Setting | Range | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| Model |  |  | Path to a YOLO ONNX model to run detection with. Required - there is nothing to draw without one. |
| Cameras |  |  | Which camera(s) to export. Runs a shorter, single-file diagnostic when only one side's tracking is in question, instead of always producing (and waiting on) both. |
| Output file |  |  | Base output path - actual files get _L/_R inserted before the extension (or just one of them, matching Cameras above). Leave empty to auto-name from the left video's filename. |
| Processing range |  |  | Trims the diagnostic to a start/end time window within the loaded clip. Defaults to the full clip. |
| Start (s) |  |  | Start time, in seconds from the beginning of the clip. |
| End (s) |  |  | End time, in seconds from the beginning of the clip. |
| Cut ranges |  |  | Excludes a time range from this diagnostic, splicing what remains back together with no gap. |
| Detect every N frames |  |  | Runs AI detection every Nth frame; frames in between reuse the last detection. Higher = cheaper but staler positions during fast action. Detection on two full-resolution raw feeds is this tool's dominant cost, so this is its biggest throughput lever. |
| Detection confidence | 0.05 to 0.9 | 0.10 | A raw detection - person, ball, or referee - below this score is not drawn. |
